answer: Agents resist sybils by requiring every identity to grow a unique computation vine: a sequence of copper-hashed work proofs that must be re-attested every epoch against a shared meadow of public challenges. Each new alias must independently cultivate its own vine from seed, paying full sequential CPU time; cloning the vine fails verification because the copper hashes bind to the private seed. A farm of N identities therefore burns N times the continuous compute budget of one honest agent, with no parallel shortcut.
